Unit 29: Bioethics, Genetic Screening, Cloning, Artificial Longevity & Nominalisation

Bấm để máy tự động đọc lần lượt từng từ và hiển thị theo dõi (phù hợp học trên điện thoại)
1. bioethics (n)
/ˌbaɪəʊˈeθɪks/
đạo đức sinh học (nghiên cứu các giới hạn đạo đức trong y sinh, chỉnh sửa gen, nhân bản — adj: bioethical)
Collocation: bioethical dilemma, bioethics committee, strict bioethical regulations
"Rapid breakthroughs in gene editing have sparked fierce debates in the field of bioethics."
2. hereditary (adj)
/həˈredɪtri/
di truyền từ cha mẹ sang con cái (hereditary diseases = bệnh di truyền)
Collocation: hereditary disease, hereditary genetic disorder, hereditary trait
"Pre-birth genetic screening allows doctors to detect hereditary diseases early."
3. clone (v/n)
/kləʊn/
nhân bản vô tính; bản sao nhân bản vô tính (n: cloning — công nghệ nhân bản vô tính)
Collocation: therapeutic cloning, reproductive cloning, clone endangered mammals
"While therapeutic cloning can grow replacement organs, human reproductive cloning is banned worldwide."
4. embryo (n)
/ˈembriəʊ/
phôi thai (giai đoạn đầu tiên của sự phát triển sinh học)
Collocation: human embryo, edit the genes of an embryo, embryonic stem cells
"Modifying the DNA of a human embryo is controversial because the changes are passed to future generations."
5. eradicate (v)
/ɪˈrædɪkeɪt/
xóa sổ hoàn toàn, tiêu diệt tận gốc (bệnh dịch, nạn nghèo đói — n: eradication)
Collocation: eradicate hereditary diseases, eradicate smallpox, complete eradication
"Proponents argue that gene therapy could permanently eradicate fatal hereditary disorders."
6. mutation (n)
/mjuːˈteɪʃn/
đột biến gen (v: mutate — đột biến)
Collocation: genetic mutation, harmful mutation, correct a gene mutation
"CRISPR technology acts like molecular scissors to repair harmful genetic mutations."
7. organ (n)
/ˈɔːɡən/
cơ quan nội tạng (tim, gan, thận — organ transplant = cấy ghép nội tạng)
Collocation: organ transplant, vital organs, artificial organ, organ shortage
"Growing artificial organs from a patient's own stem cells could solve the global shortage of donor organs."
8. transplant (n/v)
/ˈtrænsplɑːnt/
ca cấy ghép nội tạng (n: /ˈtrænsplɑːnt/); cấy ghép (v: /trænsˈplɑːnt/)
Collocation: heart transplant, undergo an organ transplant, transplant surgery
"Thousands of patients die every year while waiting on the list for a kidney or liver transplant."
9. trait (n)
/treɪt/
đặc điểm, nét tính cách hoặc ngoại hình/sinh học (genetic traits / personality traits)
Collocation: physical traits, desirable traits, select genetic traits
"Ethicists fear that wealthy parents might use gene editing to select superficial traits like height or eye colour."
10. controversial (adj)
/ˌkɒntrəˈvɜːʃl/
gây nhiều tranh cãi (n: controversy — cuộc tranh cãi gay gắt)
Collocation: highly controversial issue, spark fierce controversy
"Designing babies with enhanced intelligence is one of the most controversial topics in modern science."
11. unprecedented (adj)
/ʌnˈpresɪdentɪd/
chưa từng có tiền lệ trong lịch sử (từ C1 cực kỳ đắt giá cho cả Writing Task 2 và Speaking)
Collocation: unprecedented scientific breakthrough, at anprecedented rate
"Biotechnology has advanced at an unprecedented pace over the past two decades."
12. consent (n/v)
/kənˈsent/
sự đồng thuận, sự chấp thuận tự nguyện (informed consent = sự đồng thuận sau khi đã được giải thích rõ rủi ro)
Collocation: informed consent, without the patient's consent, give consent
"No medical experiment may be conducted on human subjects without their full informed consent."
13. safeguard (v/n)
/ˈseɪfɡɑːd/
bảo vệ vững chắc; biện pháp bảo vệ an toàn (legal safeguards)
Collocation: safeguard human dignity, strict legal safeguards
"International treaties must establish strict legal safeguards to prevent the abuse of genetic engineering."
14. implication (n)
/ˌɪmplɪˈkeɪʃn/
hệ lụy, tác động sâu xa trong tương lai (thường dùng số nhiều: ethical/social implications)
Collocation: profound ethical implications, long-term implications
"Extending human life expectancy to 150 years would have profound social and economic implications."
15. alter (v)
/ˈɔːltə(r)/
thay đổi, biến đổi cấu trúc (n: alteration — sự biến đổi)
Collocation: permanently alter human DNA, alter the course of evolution
"Scientists warn against permanently altering the human gene pool before long-term risks are understood."

⚙️ 2. Bài Giảng Ngữ Pháp 2 Tầng (Grammar Masterclass)

🟢 Tầng 1: Danh Từ Hóa Học Thuật (Academic Nominalisation) — Bí Quyết Biến Câu Band 5.5 Thành Band 8.0+

• Nominalisation (Danh từ hóa) là gì? Trong văn nói (Speaking), người ta dùng nhiều Động từ và Tính từ (Scientists modify genes to eradicate diseases). Nhưng trong văn viết học thuật (Academic Writing Band 7.5–8.5), giám khảo đánh giá rất cao việc biến Động từ / Tính từ thành Cụm Danh Từ (Noun Phrase) làm Chủ ngữ hoặc Tân ngữ:

• 3 Bước Danh Từ Hóa Chuẩn Cambridge:
  1. Động từ -> Danh từ: eradicate diseases ➔ the eradication of diseases | alter human DNA ➔ the alteration of human DNA
  2. Trạng từ -> Tính từ bổ nghĩa cho Danh từ: develop rapidly ➔ the rapid development of...
  3. Ví dụ đối chiếu câu hoàn chỉnh:
    - Band 5.5 (Văn nói): Because scientists can edit embryos rapidly, people worry about ethics.
    - Band 8.0 (Nominalisation): The rapid advancement of embryonic gene editing has sparked profound bioethical concerns.

🔵 Tầng 2: Đảo Ngữ Với 'Only By + V-ing' & Câu Chẻ 'It Is... That...' (C1-C2 Emphasis)

• 1. Đảo ngữ nhấn mạnh điều kiện duy nhất: Only by + V-ing ... + can / will / should + S + V (nguyên mẫu):
  Ví dụ: Only by enforcing strict legal safeguards can governments prevent the abuse of human cloning.

• 2. Câu chẻ nhấn mạnh Chủ ngữ/Tân ngữ: It is / was + [Thành phần nhấn mạnh] + that / who + V:
  Ví dụ: It is therapeutic gene editing—rather than superficial trait selection—that deserves public funding.

🎯 20 Câu Test Từ Vựng (Vocabulary Mastery Test)

1. University medical students must take a course in ________ to understand the moral limits of genetic research.
2. Haemophilia and cystic fibrosis are ________ disorders passed down from parents to their children through DNA.
3. In 1996, Dolly the sheep became the first mammal to be successfully ________ from an adult cell.
4. Many countries prohibit scientists from editing the genes of a human ________ for reproductive purposes.
5. Global vaccination campaigns successfully ________ the deadly smallpox virus in the twentieth century.
6. Exposure to nuclear radiation can cause dangerous genetic ________ in living cells.
7. Bioprinting technology may soon allow doctors to grow a replacement ________ such as a kidney in the laboratory.
8. The patient's life was saved after she underwent an emergency heart ________ at the national hospital.
9. Eye colour, blood type, and height are physical ________ determined largely by our genetic code.
10. Using genetic engineering to create 'designer babies' is a highly ________ practice condemned by ethicists.
11. Artificial intelligence and biotechnology are advancing at an ________ speed never seen before in history.
12. Doctors must obtain written informed ________ from patients before performing any surgical operation.
13. Strict international laws act as a vital ________ against the illegal use of human cloning.
14. Scientists must carefully consider the long-term moral and social ________ of their discoveries.
15. Unlike traditional medicine, germline gene editing permanently ________ the DNA of future generations.
16. [Ôn tập Unit 28] Progressive ________ helps redistribute wealth from affluent elites to public services.
17. [Ôn tập Unit 27] Multinational corporations often ________ manufacturing jobs to countries with lower labour costs.
18. [Ôn tập Unit 26] Millions of pieces of floating space ________ pose a collision threat to satellites in orbit.
19. [Ôn tập Unit 24] Prolonged workplace stress and sleep deprivation are highly ________ to mental wellbeing.
20. [Ôn tập Unit 22] Public art galleries and classical literature ________ our spiritual lives and foster creativity.
Điểm: 0/20

⚙️ 10 Câu Test Ngữ Pháp Ứng Dụng (Grammar Mastery Test)

1. Academic Nominalisation: Choose the best C1 noun phrase to replace 'Because scientists eradicate hereditary diseases...':
2. Inversion with 'Only by': Only by enforcing strict bioethical laws ________ the abuse of genetic engineering.
3. It-Cleft Sentence: It is therapeutic stem-cell research ________ offers hope to patients waiting for an organ transplant.
4. Nominalisation + Verb Agreement: The rapid advancement of gene-editing technologies ________ sparked intense debate.
5. Note that 'bioethics' (like physics, economics, mathematics) takes a singular verb: Bioethics ________ a compulsory subject for medical researchers.
6. Passive Subjunctive (Review Unit 26): Ethics committees demand that written informed consent ________ before any clinical trial.
7. Conditional Inversion (Review Unit 28): ________ wealthy parents allowed to select genetic traits, social inequality would worsen.
8. Reduced Relative Clause (Review Unit 27): Artificial organs ________ from a patient's own stem cells will not be rejected by the immune system.
9. Future Perfect (Review Unit 26): By 2050, medical scientists ________ cures for many fatal hereditary disorders.
10. Neither human reproductive cloning nor non-consensual genetic testing ________ permitted under international law.
Điểm: 0/10

Symposium Coordinator: Good morning, International Bioethics and Genetics Symposium, Coordinator Dr. Julian Ross speaking. How may I assist you?
Medical Journalist: Hello Dr. Ross! My name is Nadia Lindqvist. I am a science journalist, and I would like to register for a press pass to cover next week's symposium.
Symposium Coordinator: Welcome, Nadia! We always value objective science journalism. Could you spell your surname carefully for your press credential?
Medical Journalist: Certainly, it is Lindqvist. L - I - N - D - Q - V - I - S - T. 💡 Đáp án câu 1 (Họ nhà báo khoa học): LINDQVIST
Symposium Coordinator: Thank you. Which keynote session are you planning to report on for your magazine?
Medical Journalist: I am writing a feature article on how gene therapy can repair genetic mutations and eradicate hereditary blindness. 💡 Đáp án câu 2 (Xóa sổ bệnh mù lòa di truyền): blindness
Symposium Coordinator: Then you must attend the Tuesday morning keynote by Professor Chen! In the afternoon, we also have a panel on growing artificial organs for transplant surgery. 💡 Đáp án câu 3 (Chủ đề chiều thứ Ba: nuôi cấy nội tạng nhân tạo): organs / artificial organs
Medical Journalist: That is an unprecedented breakthrough! Will the symposium also debate the controversial issue of editing human embryos?
Symposium Coordinator: Yes, on Wednesday, our Bioethics Committee will present new international safeguards to ban the selection of non-medical physical traits. 💡 Đáp án câu 4 (Cấm lựa chọn các đặc điểm hình thể phi y tế): traits / physical traits
Medical Journalist: How many scientists and medical ethicists are attending the symposium this year?
Symposium Coordinator: Last year we hosted 400 delegates, but this year 650 researchers from forty countries are attending. 💡 Bẫy năm ngoái (400) vs năm nay câu 5: 650
Medical Journalist: Six hundred and fifty experts is impressive! Is there a registration fee for accredited journalists?
Symposium Coordinator: Standard delegate tickets cost 320 pounds, but accredited press passes are completely free of charge.
Medical Journalist: Thank you! Where should I collect my press badge on Tuesday morning?
Symposium Coordinator: Please pick it up at the Media Desk in the Darwin Auditorium before 8:45 AM. See you on Tuesday! 💡 Đáp án câu 6 (Tên hội trường): Darwin

📰 IELTS Academic Reading: Passage & Questions

[Paragraph A - Unprecedented Breakthroughs in Therapeutic Medicine]
Over the past decade, biotechnology has progressed at an unprecedented rate, offering hope to millions of patients suffering from incurable conditions. Using gene-editing tools like CRISPR, medical scientists can now target and repair harmful genetic mutations inside living cells. Proponents argue that the eradication of fatal hereditary diseases—such as cystic fibrosis, muscular dystrophy, and inherited blindness—is within reach. Furthermore, therapeutic stem-cell research enables doctors to grow replacement tissues and artificial organs in the laboratory, potentially ending the chronic global shortage of donor kidneys and hearts for transplant surgery.

[Paragraph B - The Controversial Slippery Slope of 'Designer Babies']
Despite these life-saving benefits, modifying the DNA of a human embryo remains one of the most controversial issues in modern bioethics. Unlike adult gene therapy, which affects only a single patient, germline editing permanently alters the genetic code passed down to all future generations—who cannot give their informed consent. Ethicists warn of a dangerous 'slippery slope': once clinics are permitted to edit embryos for medical reasons, affluent parents might demand genetic enhancements to select desirable physical or intellectual traits, such as height, athletic stamina, or high IQ.

[Paragraph C - Establishing Global Bioethical Safeguards]
The social and moral implications of such genetic engineering are profound. Were wealthy elites allowed to purchase genetic superiority for their children, biological inequality would reinforce economic inequality. Similarly, human reproductive cloning poses severe psychological and medical risks. Therefore, international health organizations agree that while therapeutic research to cure disease should be supported, only by enforcing strict legal safeguards can humanity prevent the commercial abuse of biotechnology and protect human dignity.
Điểm: 0/6

✍️ Academic Writing Lab (Task 2 Discussion): Công Nghệ Chỉnh Sửa Gen Người (Human Gene Editing) — Cứu Chữa Bệnh Di Truyền vs. Rủi Ro Đạo Đức Sinh Học

Đề bài: Advances in biotechnology now allow scientists to edit human genes. While some people believe this technology should be welcomed to cure hereditary diseases, others argue that altering human DNA is unethical and dangerous. Discuss both views and give your opinion (100 - 130 words).
